# aidial_application (Resource)

Manages an application in DIAL Core (`PUT /v1/applications/{bucket}/{path}`). An application is either endpoint-based (`endpoint`) or schema-based (`application_type_schema_id` with `application_properties`); DIAL Core rejects both together. Fields this resource does not model, such as code-based applications (`function`), are not managed: a PUT replaces the whole document, so they are dropped on the next apply. Do not manage `function` applications with this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An endpoint-based application.
resource "aidial_application" "example" {
  bucket       = "platform"
  path         = "my-application"
  display_name = "Support assistant"
  description  = "Answers questions about the product"
  endpoint     = "https://application.example.invalid/chat"

  forward_auth_token = true
  max_retry_attempts = 2
  interceptors       = ["my-interceptor"]

  default_headers = {
    "X-Team" = "platform"
  }
}

# A schema-based application: no endpoint, typed by an application type schema.
resource "aidial_application" "typed" {
  bucket                     = "platform"
  path                       = "my-typed-application"
  application_type_schema_id = aidial_application_type_schema.example.schema_id

  application_properties = {
    prompt = "You are a helpful assistant."
  }
}

# An application with MCP, its own routes and an OAuth external service.
resource "aidial_application" "full" {
  bucket   = "platform"
  path     = "my-full-application"
  endpoint = "https://application.example.invalid/chat"

  input_attachment_types = ["*/*"]
  description_keywords   = ["support"]
  dependencies           = ["my-model"]

  mcp = {
    endpoint  = "https://application.example.invalid/mcp"
    transport = "HTTP"
  }

  routes = {
    health = {
      paths = ["/health"]
      response = {
        status = 200
        body   = "ok"
      }
    }
  }

  allow_user_external_services = true
  external_services = {
    crm = {
      display_name = "CRM"
      auth_settings = {
        authentication_type    = "OAUTH"
        client_id              = "my-client"
        client_secret          = var.crm_client_secret # at least 8 characters, never read back from DIAL Core
        authorization_endpoint = "https://crm.example.invalid/authorize"
        token_endpoint         = "https://crm.example.invalid/token"
      }
    }
  }
}

variable "crm_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `bucket` (String) Target DIAL bucket, for example `platform` or `public`.
- `path` (String) Application path inside the bucket. `/` separates folders; DIAL Core accepts `/` only in the `public` bucket.

### Optional

- `allow_user_external_services` (Boolean) Allow users to add their own external services to the application.
- `application_properties` (Dynamic) Values for the properties of the application type schema (free-form object, sent to DIAL as-is).
- `application_type_schema_id` (String) URI (`$id`) of the application type schema, for example the `schema_id` of an `aidial_application_type_schema`. Schema-based applications take no `endpoint`.
- `base_url` (String) Application-level base URL that completes `interfaces` entries without their own `base_url`.
- `catalog_properties` (Dynamic) Catalog metadata of the application (free-form object).
- `catalog_schema_id` (String) URI (`$id`) of the catalog schema describing `catalog_properties`, for example the `schema_id` of an `aidial_catalog_schema`.
- `default_headers` (Map of String) Additional headers sent with every request to the application's endpoint.
- `defaults` (Dynamic) Default request parameters (free-form object, sent to DIAL as-is).
- `dependencies` (Set of String) Deployments the application depends on. DIAL Core defaults to none.
- `description` (String) Application description.
- `description_keywords` (Set of String) Keywords describing the application. DIAL Core defaults to none.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable application name.
- `display_version` (String) Version shown for the application.
- `editor_url` (String) URL of the application editor.
- `endpoint` (String) URL DIAL Core calls to run the application. Set exactly one of `endpoint` and `application_type_schema_id`.
- `external_services` (Attributes Map) External services the application can use, keyed by service name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--external_services))
- `features` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--features))
- `forward_auth_token` (Boolean) Forward the caller's authorization token to the application. DIAL Core defaults to false.
- `icon_url` (String) URL of the application icon.
- `input_attachment_types` (Set of String) MIME types of accepted input attachments.
- `interceptors` (Set of String) Names of interceptors applied to the application's requests. DIAL Core defaults to none.
- `interfaces` (Attributes Map) Per-interface deployment configuration, keyed by DIAL Core interface type: `openaiChatCompletions`, `openaiEmbeddings`, `openaiResponses`, `anthropicMessages`. The keys are Core's camelCase names and are sent as written; the attributes inside each entry use snake_case. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces))
- `intro` (String) Introductory text shown for the application.
- `max_input_attachments` (Number) Maximum number of attachments in one request.
- `max_retry_attempts` (Number) Maximum number of retry attempts. DIAL Core defaults to 1.
- `mcp` (Attributes) MCP settings of the application. Removing it removes MCP from the application. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mcp))
- `name` (String) Application name sent in the DIAL API request body. DIAL Core derives the name from the bucket and path, so it can be omitted; then it is read back from the API.
- `override_name` (String) Override of the application name presented to clients.
- `reference` (String) Reference identifier of the application. DIAL Core generates one when it is not set.
- `responses_defaults` (Dynamic) Default request parameters for Responses API requests (free-form object, sent to DIAL as-is).
- `responses_endpoint` (String) Endpoint used for Responses API requests.
- `routes` (Attributes Map) Routes of the application, keyed by route name. DIAL Core fills `order`, `methods`, `permissions`, `max_retry_attempts` and similar fields in when they are not set. Set `routes = {}` to remove all routes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes))
- `user_roles` (Set of String) Roles allowed to use the application.
- `viewer_url` (String) URL of the application viewer.

### Read-Only

- `api_name` (String) Canonical application name returned by the DIAL API.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier in the form <bucket>/<path>.

<a id="nestedatt--external_services"></a>
### Nested Schema for `external_services`

Optional:

- `auth_settings` (Attributes) Authentication settings of the service. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--external_services--auth_settings))
- `description` (String) Service description.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable service name.

<a id="nestedatt--external_services--auth_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `external_services.auth_settings`

Optional:

- `api_key_header` (String) Header that carries the API key.
- `authentication_type` (String) Authentication type: `OAUTH`, `API_KEY`, `NONE` or `DIAL_NATIVE`. DIAL Core validates which other fields it accepts.
- `authorization_endpoint` (String) OAuth authorization endpoint.
- `client_id` (String) OAuth client ID.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) OAuth client secret, at least 8 characters. DIAL Core never returns it, so state keeps the configured value; after import it is null.
- `code_verifier` (String, Sensitive) PKCE code verifier. DIAL Core never returns it and rejects it for some authentication types.
- `scopes_supported` (Set of String) OAuth scopes.
- `token_endpoint` (String) OAuth token endpoint.

<a id="nestedatt--interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces`

Optional:

- `base_url` (String)
- `default_headers` (Map of String) Additional headers sent with every request served by this interface.
- `mode` (String) `passthrough` (default) or `translator`.
- `override_paths` (Map of String) Overrides of the paths appended to the interface base URL.


<a id="nestedatt--mcp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mcp`

Optional:

- `allowed_tools` (Set of String) Names of the MCP tools exposed. An empty set, which DIAL Core defaults to, exposes all of them.
- `config_delivery` (String) How the configuration is delivered: `HEADER` or `META`. DIAL Core defaults to `META`.
- `endpoint` (String) MCP endpoint of the application.
- `forward_per_request_key` (Boolean) Forward the per-request key to the MCP endpoint. DIAL Core defaults to true.
- `mcp_apps` (Attributes) MCP apps settings. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mcp--mcp_apps))
- `transport` (String) MCP transport: `HTTP` or `SSE`. DIAL Core defaults to `HTTP`.

<a id="nestedatt--mcp--mcp_apps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mcp.mcp_apps`

Optional:

- `domain_override` (String) Domain override for MCP apps.



<a id="nestedatt--routes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes`

Optional:

- `attachment_paths` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--attachment_paths))
- `max_retry_attempts` (Number) Maximum number of retry attempts.
- `methods` (Set of String) HTTP methods the route matches.
- `order` (Number) Route matching order.
- `paths` (Set of String) Path patterns the route matches.
- `permissions` (Set of String) Permissions of the route.
- `response` (Attributes) Static response returned by the route instead of forwarding upstream. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--response))
- `rewrite_path` (Boolean)
- `upstreams` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--upstreams))
- `user_roles` (Set of String) Roles allowed to use the route.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--attachment_paths"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.attachment_paths`

Optional:

- `request_body` (Set of String) Request body paths that carry attachments.
- `response_body` (Set of String) Response body paths that carry attachments.


<a id="nestedatt--routes--response"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.response`

Optional:

- `body` (String)
- `status` (Number)


<a id="nestedatt--routes--upstreams"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.upstreams`

Required:

- `endpoint` (String)
- `tier` (Number)
- `weight` (Number)

Optional:

- `auth_header_name` (String) Name of the HTTP header that carries the key. Required when `auth_type` is `CUSTOM_HEADER`, not allowed otherwise.
- `auth_type` (String) How the key is sent to the upstream: `API_KEY`, `BEARER` or `CUSTOM_HEADER`. `CUSTOM_HEADER` requires `auth_header_name` and needs DIAL Core 0.50 or newer.
- `base_url` (String)
- `extra_data` (Map of String)
- `id` (String)
- `key` (String, Sensitive) Upstream key. DIAL Core never returns it, so state keeps the configured value.
- `responses_endpoint` (String)
- `secret_extra_data` (Map of String, Sensitive)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = aidial_application.example
  id = "platform/my-application"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <bucket>/<path>. The bucket is "platform" or "public"; the path may contain "/".
terraform import aidial_application.example platform/my-application
```
